Attacks on Ukrainian energy and railway infrastructure were being made possible ⁠partly due to restrictions on Ukraine’s use of Elon Musk’s Starshield service, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Sunday – reiterating criticism he made late last week. “Many of these ‌strikes are getting through because restrictions on the speed of Starshield terminals along the frontline in the temporarily occupied territories are still there.” The president said Russian forces were singling out ​specific regions – in particular, southeastern Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia – and repeatedly striking them over several days. There have ​been many outages, and restoration ​is proceeding,” he ‌said. “Power has ​been ​restored to some extent, but there is still a lot of work ahead.”

Zelenskyy made similar
title: Ukraine war briefing: Energy attacks made possible by continuing Starshield restrictions, says Zelenskyy

author: Associated Press
description:
Pontiff delivers forceful speech on final day in Peru as he travels from high in the Andes into the Amazon

Pope Leo XIV has demanded justice for environmental defenders killed for protecting the Amazon and backed efforts by Indigenous peoples to stop their lands from being ravaged by logging and illegal mining.

On the penultimate day of his South American tour, Leo on Sunday travelled into the Peruvian Amazon and channelled one of Pope Francis’s core teachings that links care for the most vulnerable with care for God’s creation.

Continue reading...
title: ‘The blood of these brothers cries out’: Pope Leo demands justice for people killed protecting the Amazon

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Silicon Valley figures back CEO ousted after revelations of affair with suspected Chinese spy, as US treasury secretary urges Nvidia to carry out ‘dramatic shake-up’

Elon Musk and a host of other tech executives are among more than 158,000 signatories of an open letter calling for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia chief, days after he resigned from the multi-trillion dollar chip company.

The letter demands that the company’s board members “bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts”.

Continue reading...
title: Elon Musk joins 158,000 others calling for Nvidia to bring back Jensen Huang in open letter

author: Giles Richards
description:
• Former champion calls for more equality in recruitment

  • ‘Inspiration means nothing without opportunity’

Lewis Hamilton has demanded Formula One does more to deliver on diversity and inclusion, warning that the future of the sport is dependent on taking robust action to address inequality in recruitment.

Hamilton has called on F1 to make greater investments, more extensive recording and publishing of data of who is in the sport and a commitment from teams to guarantee a number of paid early-career places for young people from underrepresented backgrounds.

Continue reading...
title: Lewis Hamilton urges F1 to ‘push harder and move faster’ on diversity

author: Lyndsey Winship
description:
Exclusive: Trailer released for Rambert’s version of Russell T Davies’s show about friendship amid the 80s Aids crisis and the ‘extraordinary freedom’ of clubbing

Russell T Davies’s award-winning series It’s a Sin, about young gay friends living through the Aids crisis in 1980s London, is getting a new life as a dance piece, with a trailer released on Monday ahead of an opening at Aviva Studios in Manchester in February.

“We had a few approaches, but a lot of people wanted to make it a musical, which made my heart sink slightly,” said Davies. “I always imagined an aria between those two women on the seafront at the end and I thought: ‘Oh, that could be so terrible!’” Dance was different, he said. “It felt so original and so pure. The story distils down to these emotional moments that are going to be done so beautifu
title: ‘Loaded with potential’: stage version of TV smash It’s a Sin has the dancefloor at its heart

author: Harry Taylor
description:
Calls for governments to recognise sexual exploitation of children as preventable public health emergency

Reports of artificial intelligence being used to sexually exploit children have risen by more than 8,400% in two years, research has found.

A report by the Edinburgh-based Childlight – Global Child Safety Institute says AI-related child abuse material, including deepfakes using “nudify apps”, had risen from about 4,700 in 2023 to more than 400,000 in 2025.

Continue reading...
title: Reports of AI-related child sexual abuse material rise 8,400% in two years, data shows
